    def run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
        previous_mode = view.model.training
        view.model.eval()
        diagnostic_rng = local_generator(seed=42)
        try:
            with no_grad():
                record_actual_convolutions_and_reachable_offset_sets()
                collect_existing_embedding_and_all_position_margin_metrics()
                for batch in fixed_bounded_batches(train_loader):
                    _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
                    t, nonempty = largest_nonzero_index_per_row(sequence)
                    valid = nonempty & nonzero_targets_at(positive, negative, t)
                    targets = paired_items_at_original_t(positive, negative, t)
                    base = score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(sequence, targets)
                    record_final_pair_margins_and_negative_wins(base, valid)

                    recent_slots, older_slots, eligible = matched_disjoint_slots(
                        sequence, m=lambda n: min(3, (n - 1) // 2), keep_final=True)
                    for selected_slots in [recent_slots, older_slots]:
                        repacked = delete_selected_events_and_left_pad(sequence, selected_slots)
                        packed_scores = score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(repacked, targets)
                        with temporary_embedding_output_ablation(selected_slots):
                            fixed_scores = score_at_original_readout(sequence, targets, t)
                        record_paired_changes(base, packed_scores, fixed_scores,
                                              valid & eligible)

                    for draw in range(5):
                        shuffled, eligible = shuffle_valid_prefix_keep_final(
                            sequence, diagnostic_rng)
                        record_nonidentity_shuffle_support(eligible)
                        record_paired_changes(base,
                            score_original_targets_at_last_nonpadding(shuffled, targets),
                            valid=valid & eligible)

                    check_future_changes_leave_features_through_t_unchanged(sequence)
                    check_aligned_prefix_equivalence(sequence)
                    probe_recorded_reachable_and_unreachable_offsets(sequence)

                return {'metrics': summarize_with_support_nulls_and_configuration(),
                        'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions_and_limits()}
        finally:
            remove_any_remaining_diagnostic_hooks()
            view.model.train(previous_mode)

The recommended first experiment remains **position-dependent gating over NextItNet dilation depths**, trained jointly within one model per category. This is an incremental hypothesis; no validation improvement has been measured.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users report that older, isolated purchases overshadow coherent recent behavior. Adaptive context weighting could reduce this mismatch, but does not guarantee historical exclusion. (2) Broad matches displace specific purpose or mood matches. Context selection may sharpen immediate intent; it cannot establish compatibility or distinguish complements from redundant purchases without sufficient evidence. (3) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 lower-tail margin. Embedding similarity scores near 0.5 indicate mean pairwise cosine similarity near zero, providing no strong evidence of directional collapse; contextual discrimination is therefore a better-supported target than dispersion regularization.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) supplies causal multiscale features. [TV-Rec](https://openreview.net/pdf/e9c3bd1680a3ab54ffe119fc526e57d9835d7b8d.pdf) motivates adaptive convolutional processing without establishing gains here. (2) [Dynamic Layer Aggregation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.05770) closely precedes position-wise depth fusion; [SkipRec](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/16518) supplies recommendation-specific adaptive depth. Novelty is consequently limited. (3) [Sampled-softmax research](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivates moderate-temperature negative competition; [semantic fusion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) motivates separate treatment of text and IDs. Neither establishes practical compatibility from available data.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Context selection targets stale intent; objective design targets confusing candidates; content integration targets item identity. These address different information gaps and should initially be tested separately.

Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell includes a positive and negative consideration. Alignment scores express hypotheses, not observed gains.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Learned dilation-depth gates | 3: focused convolutional adaptation / close precedents | 6: adaptable context / no guaranteed cutoff | 7: targets stale interests and broad matches / cannot verify fit | 6: contextual discrimination / weak margins may persist | 4: compact module / controls and serialization required |
| Moderate-temperature multi-negative loss | 3: focused objective change / established technique | 7: candidate competition / latent false negatives | 5: finer ranking / no explicit intent control | 9: targets weak separation / sampled gains may not generalize | 4: reusable scoring / exclusion bookkeeping |
| Joint scratch-trained title/ID gate | 5: constrained fusion / established ingredients | 6: identifiable cues / sparse text supervision | 7: specificity / similarity cannot establish compatibility | 6: extra discrimination / noisy features | 6: no external weights / tokenization overhead |

**Selected algorithm.** At 0% progress, retain depth gating as a small, testable intervention addressing two user failures: stale-interest persistence and broad matches displacing recent purpose-specific choices. It also targets Electronics’ weak separation. Multi-negative training is a strong subsequent alternative, but changing both would obscure attribution.

Retain causal residual blocks; consistently normalize their outputs and learn position-wise softmax depth weights initialized uniformly. Deep gate inputs can preserve dependence on old interactions even when shallow weights dominate. Test historical sensitivity through prefix perturbations; do not interpret weights as intent explanations.

Compare final-block readout, uniform fusion, learned fusion, and a parameter-matched final-block head as separate trials within budget. Hold other settings fixed; report all category HR@10 values, gate entropy/usage, parameters, training time, and peak GPU memory. Predeclare validation checkpoints and stopping rules, log every query, and freeze selection before hidden evaluation. If host-provided per-user hits are available, paired user bootstraps can describe conditional uncertainty; winner intervals remain exploratory and sampled-candidate HR does not establish full-catalog performance.

Preserve seeds, all four routes, fixed splits/evaluator, ≤200 epochs, 200 batches/epoch, diagnostic interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. hyper-parameter profile across datasets. The generated predict.py routes by the
optional dataset_name keyword used by the RecHarness Amazon Reviews harness.

]

def _read_split(path: str) -> dict[int, list[int]]:
    data: dict[int, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        return {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            parts = line.strip().split()
            if len(parts) == 2:
                data[int(parts[0])].append(int(parts[1]))
    return dict(data)


def _load_itemnum(data_dir: str, dataset_name: str) -> int:
    stats_path = os.path.join(data_dir, "dataset_stats.json")
    if os.path.isfile(stats_path):
        with open(stats_path) as f:
            stats = json.load(f)
        if dataset_name in stats:
            return int(stats[dataset_name]["itemnum"])
    itemnum = 0
    for split in ("train", "valid"):
        path = os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_{split}.txt")
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            for line in f:
                parts = line.strip().split()
                if len(parts) == 2:
                    itemnum = max(itemnum, int(parts[1]))
    return itemnum


def load_dataset(dataset_name: str, data_dir: str):
    user_train = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_train.txt"))
    user_valid = _read_split(os.path.join(data_dir, f"{dataset_name}_valid.txt"))
    itemnum = _load_itemnum(data_dir, dataset_name)
    return user_train, user_valid, itemnum

def bpr_sequence_loss(
    model: nn.Module, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor
) -> torch.Tensor:
    pos_scores, neg_scores = model(seq, pos, neg)
    mask = (pos != 0).float()
    loss = -torch.log(torch.sigmoid(pos_scores - neg_scores) + 1e-8)
    return (loss * mask).sum() / mask.sum().clamp(min=1.0)

class NextItNetBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(
        self, hidden_units: int, dilation: int, kernel_size: int, dropout_rate: float
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.dilation = dilation
        self.kernel_size = kernel_size
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv1d(
            hidden_units, hidden_units, kernel_size, dilation=dilation, padding=0
        )
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_units)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout_rate)
        self.activation = nn.GELU()

    def _causal_conv(self, conv: nn.Conv1d, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        pad = (self.kernel_size - 1) * self.dilation
        x = nn.functional.pad(x, (pad, 0))
        return conv(x)

    ### >>> Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-START: Mask every causal convolution sublayer to prevent padding contamination
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, valid: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        mask = valid.unsqueeze(-1).to(x.dtype)
        residual = x * mask
        y = (self.norm1(residual) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv1, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        y = self.dropout(self.activation(y)) * mask
        y = (self.norm2(y) * mask).transpose(1, 2)
        y = self._causal_conv(self.conv2, y).transpose(1, 2) * mask
        y = self.dropout(y) * mask
        return (residual + y) * mask

    ### <<< Self_EvolveRec-BLOCK-END

            nn.init.zeros_(self.depth_gate.bias)

    def forward(self, seq: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, neg: torch.Tensor):

        return pos_scores, neg_scores

        self, seq: torch.Tensor, candidates: torch.Tensor
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        out = self.encode_sequence(seq)

        for _ in range(NUM_BATCHES):

    @staticmethod
    def _last(sequence):
        indices = torch.arange(sequence.size(1), device=sequence.device).expand_as(
            sequence
        )
        last = indices.masked_fill(sequence.eq(0), -1).amax(dim=1)
        return last.clamp(min=0), last.ge(0)

    def _features(self, sequence, ablate=None):
        if ablate is None:
            return self.model.log2feats(sequence)

        def hook(module, args, output):
            if output.shape[:-1] != ablate.shape:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    "unexpected embedding shape during diagnostic ablation"
                )
            return output * (~ablate).unsqueeze(-1).to(output.dtype)

        handle = self.model.item_emb.register_forward_hook(hook)
        self._hooks.append(handle)
        try:
            return self.model.log2feats(sequence)
        finally:
            handle.remove()
            self._hooks.remove(handle)

    def _scores(self, sequence, targets, ablate=None):
        # The hook is removed before target embeddings are looked up.
        features = self._features(sequence, ablate)
        last, nonempty = self._last(sequence)
        rows = torch.arange(sequence.size(0), device=sequence.device)
        final = features[rows, last] * nonempty.unsqueeze(-1).to(features.dtype)
        return self.model.predict_score(final, targets)

    def _structure(self):
        net = self.network
        records, reachable = [], {0}
        limitations = []
        blocks = getattr(net, "blocks", [])
        if not blocks or type(net).__name__ != "NextItNetModel":
            limitations.append("unrecognized backbone topology")
        for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
            branch = set(reachable)
            for name in ("conv1", "conv2"):
                conv = getattr(block, name, None)
                if not isinstance(conv, torch.nn.Conv1d):
                    limitations.append(f"blocks.{index}.{name} is not Conv1d")
                    continue
                k, d, stride = conv.kernel_size[0], conv.dilation[0], conv.stride[0]
                records.append(
                    {
                        "name": f"blocks.{index}.{name}",
                        "kernel": k,
                        "dilation": d,
                        "stride": stride,
                        "module_padding": list(conv.padding),
                    }
                )
                if stride != 1 or conv.padding != (0,):
                    limitations.append(
                        "unsupported stride or internal convolution padding"
                    )
                branch = {s + j * d for s in branch for j in range(k)}
            reachable |= branch
        known_containers = {id(net), *(id(block) for block in blocks)}
        allowed = (
            torch.nn.ModuleList,
            torch.nn.Conv1d,
            torch.nn.Embedding,
            torch.nn.Linear,
            torch.nn.Dropout,
            torch.nn.GELU,
            torch.nn.LayerNorm,
        )
        for name, module in net.named_modules():
            if id(module) not in known_containers and not isinstance(module, allowed):
                limitations.append(
                    f"dependency analysis required for {name}: {type(module).__name__}"
                )
            if isinstance(module, torch.nn.LayerNorm):
                if tuple(module.normalized_shape) != (net.hidden_units,):
                    limitations.append(f"non-channel-only normalization: {name}")
        if len(records) != sum(isinstance(m, torch.nn.Conv1d) for m in net.modules()):
            limitations.append("convolutions outside the recognized residual branches")
        verified = bool(records) and not limitations
        return {
            "analysis": "supplied causal residual topology; empirical checks reported separately",
            "convolutions": records,
            "reachable_offsets": sorted(reachable) if verified else None,
            "maximum_offset": max(reachable) if verified else None,
            "span": max(reachable) + 1 if verified else None,
            "limitations": limitations,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _summary(values):
        if not values:
            return {
                "comparisons": 0,
                "mean": None,
                "p10": None,
                "neg_beats_pos_rate": None,
                "small_margin_rate": None,
            }
        x = torch.cat(values).float()
        return {
            "comparisons": x.numel(),
            "mean": x.mean().item(),
            "p10": x.kthvalue(max(1, int(np.ceil(0.1 * x.numel())))).values.item(),
            "neg_beats_pos_rate": (x < 0).float().mean().item(),
            "small_margin_rate": (x < 0.5).float().mean().item(),
